headlines.summary: A24 films "Backrooms," "The Drama" and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary, "You Can See Everything," are fueling a banner year at the box office.
headlines.article_text: A24’s box office success could give HBO Max a streaming edge Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points A24 films "Backrooms," "The Drama" and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary, "You Can See Everything," are fueling a banner year at the box office for the independent movie studio. Newly released A24 films are available on HBO Max after their theatrical runs due to a licensing agreement that was renewed earlier this year. HBO Max parent Skydance is seeking to increase its streaming subscribers and eventually merge the service with Paramount+. In this article SKYD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A still from the A24 film "You Can See Everything." Source: A24 Independent movie studio A24 has had a banner year at the box office, and HBO Max is set up to benefit from its success. Subscribers to the Skydance -owned streaming service can watch newly released A24 films for a limited period of time after they leave theaters thanks to a licensing deal that the studio and streamer renewed in January. A24 is behind some of this year's buzziest films, including horror hit "Backrooms," dark comedy "The Drama" starring Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything," co-directed by Nathan Fielder. The studio has generated more than $526 million at the domestic box office this year as of Nov. 15, according to data from Rentrak. That's already roughly $290 million, or more than 50%, above its haul for all of 2025. "They have an identity all their own, and just the mere mention of A24, the recognition that a movie is from A24, gives it instant credibility and provides a must-see factor, no matter what the subject matter," Paul Dergarabedian, head of marketplace trends at Rentrak, told CNBC. The strong performance for A24 comes at a critical moment for HBO Max as the newly merged Skydance seeks to boost its streaming subscriber count and bolster its edge against competitors — while managing nearly $80 billion of debt. Skydance co-CEO and Chairman David Ellison cited movie releases from A24 as part of the company's "unmatched portfolio" during its most recent earnings call. The agreement between A24 and HBO Max gives U.S. subscribers exclusive access to new films after their theatrical runs as well as some older titles from A24's library. The partnership was first negotiated in December 2023 after A24's deal with Showtime expired. A24 films released this year broke records at the box office, with "Backrooms" becoming the studio's biggest domestic opening to date and "You Can See Everything" notching the biggest documentary opening since "Fahrenheit 9/11" in 2004. That success has already begun to translate to HBO Max's platform. When "Backrooms" began streaming on HBO Max, it was the most streamed title on the platform for two weeks, according to Nielsen data. The film was also the fourth overall most streamed title the week it premiered, racking up 226 million minutes of viewing time. Among HBO Max's domestic subscribers, nearly 70% of viewers who watched at least one A24 movie in 2025 watched an average of four films from the studio, according to HBO Max and A24. A new era for HBO Max After more than a year of competing bids and regulatory hurdles , Skydance now oversees two of the world's largest streaming platforms: HBO Max and Paramount+. The company plans to eventually merge the streaming services into a single platform. It will take the first step in that effort by offering a value bundle in early 2027 . The combination of the platforms "will drive stronger engagement and higher lifetime value," co-CEO Ynon Kreiz said on the company's earnings call earlier this month. Paramount Skydance's direct-to-consumer segment, which includes Paramount+ and its free, ad-supported channel, Pluto TV, generated more than $2 billion in revenue during the third quarter, representing more than 35% of total revenue for the period. That segment revenue marked an 11% year-over-year increase, with revenue from Paramount+ up 21%. The earnings do not reflect the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, since that deal closed after the close of the quarter. Paramount Skydance's third-quarter studio revenue, meanwhile, improved 23% year over year, generating $1.5 billion. TV media revenue declined 7% year over year to $3 billion as the linear business faces headwinds related to lower advertising revenue and pay TV subscriber losses. Revenue growth in streaming will be important as it faces the daunting task of managing nearly $80 billion of debt. The company has said it expects to realize $6 billion in cost savings over the next three years and has put a particular focus on consolidating its operations and streamlining its marketing spend. Paramount+, HBO and HBO Max currently reach a combined 203 million subscribers, Ellison said during the third-quarter earnings call. Industry leader Netflix reported 325 million subscribers as of the fourth quarter of 2025, its most recent update. Disney+ and Hulu reported a combined 195.7 million subscribers as of the same period.
